claude.sample_unit: machine learning models (laboratory result classifiers) silently deployed
models_evaluated: Random forest binary classifiers (12 laboratory result prediction models)

links.outcome: Prospective silent-trial AUROC versus retrospective AUROC
links.effect: Silent deployment revealed prospective AUROC generally several points lower than retrospective, e.g., sodium 0.79 vs 0.71, white blood cell 0.76 vs 0.69, carbon dioxide 0.69 vs 0.62.
links.quote: Our silent trial results underscore the necessity of prospective evaluations before ML applications are integrated into clinical work-streams.

links.outcome: Performance gap detected by shadow deployment on live EMR data
links.effect: Across 12 models, prospective AUROC was lower than retrospective, e.g., hemoglobin 0.88 vs 0.83, potassium 0.67 vs 0.60; authors recommend prospective silent-trial estimates for go decisions.
links.quote: Across our 12 laboratory predictions tasks, AUROC in our prospective test sets were generally several percentage points lower than what is seen retrospectively.

links.outcome: Model performance by number of available features at inference
links.effect: Performance increased with number of available features at inference time; missing data degraded performance in production.
links.quote: We show that performance of our ML models increases with the number of available features at inference time.

unlisted_practices: Randomization injected into inference display to estimate model impact and correct feedback-loop bias in monitoring

models_evaluated: Random forest classifiers predicting abnormal laboratory results (12 models)

links.outcome: Retrospective versus prospective AUROC during silent deployment
links.effect: Retrospective versus prospective AUROC: white blood cell, 0.76 [0.74, 0.79] versus 0.69 [0.68, 0.70]; sodium, 0.79 [0.75, 0.82] versus 0.71 [0.70, 0.72].
links.quote: Across our 12 laboratory predictions tasks, AUROC in our prospective test sets were generally several percentage points lower than what is seen retrospectively.

links.outcome: Model performance stratified by available feature count
links.effect: Performance increased with the number of available features at inference time; numerical effect estimates were not provided in the text.
links.quote: We show that performance of our ML models increases with the number of available features at inference time.

links.effect: AUROC in prospective test sets was generally several percentage points lower than in retrospective test sets
links.quote: Across our 12 laboratory predictions tasks, AUROC in our prospective test sets were generally several percentage points lower than what is seen retrospectively.

links.quote: Across our 12 laboratory predictions tasks, AUROC in our prospective test sets were generally several percentage points lower than what is seen retrospectively.

screen.reason: Evaluates a deployment framework and demonstrates silent-mode live prospective evaluation of 12 clinical risk/lab prediction models in an EMR system to assess performance discrepancies from retrospective estimates.
